slots.text:
Hextech Rocketbelt is Mordekaiser's best option 
when it comes to getting into range to procc all 
of your abilities.

It also simultaneously holds itself as an item 
that can apply different item effects such as 
Cosmic Drive or Rylai's to get into range,

Or Riftmaker / Liandry's to start ramping
up your damage before you reach them.

And, it can also obviously help out with applying 
different items such as Experimental Hexplate or 
Hextech Gunblade, that require you to get 
an initial amount of range because well- 
you're using Rocketbelt's dash.

Additionally, it can also be used as an auto reset.

It also helps that its build path is one of the best
build paths you can possibly get for Mordekaiser
specifically with its cheap item components
and generally great stats.
This item is viable as a second item.
This item is viable as a third item.

Don't go Anti-kite items after your third item.

You probably should've went them before your fourth item if you're
having issues with catching up with the enemy team.

Rylai's with Approach Velocity is the only time
when you should ever run Rylai's as your first
item ever.

This is because the item, by itself, sucks.

Not only is it hard countered by dashes, but it
also provides zero combat value in its effect 
which is exceptionally dangerous to go 
without of in the modern era of league where
everybody (including a lot of tanks) have some
sort of threat potential.

The only reason why I'm including Rylai's with
approach velocity here is because there are
some matchups whose only win condition
against you is running away from you instead 
of fighting you such as Dr. Mundo, Vladimir, 
Ryze, etc. where you need the pseudo cosmic 
drive that comes with approach velocity and 
the slow to consistently keep up with them.

And if you say that you need Rylai's by
itself to land your skillshots, then: skill issue.

Or get Dusk & Dawn which doesn't even 
require you to land your skillshot in the first 
place.

We are not in the dark ages anymore where
our only options are to either go Riftmaker or
Rylai's.

;We can build other items now, and that's a
good thing!

Cosmic drive, as a second item, is a lot
better than it is as a first item.

This is because it's high amounts of 
ability haste serves itself as an enabler
as opposed to a raw source of output.

Now, the two scenarios where you would
go Cosmic Drive in order to consistently
keep up with the enemy team comp,

(Note: Cosmic Drive is not a good item
for getting into range since it needs you
to hit the enemy first to apply it; that's
what rocketbelt is for)

Is either: 

1. You built rocketbelt because your
enemy laner was ranged and you need
extra mobility for their ranged centric
composition

or

2. You built Riftmaker / Dusk & Dawn as
a rush item and, again: need extra 
mobility to keep up with the enemy team
comp.

Both of which are good scenarios for
cosmic drive because you either straight
up don't need an additional damage source
because the enemy team comp is far too
squishy,

or

You already have a damage item for 
cosmic drive to play off of.

And therefore: you can utilize it's ability
haste and movement speed to great
value.

Additionally: this item synergizes 
exceptionally well with any form of damage
over time effect that you can get your 
hands on such as Deathfire Touch, 
Fated Ashes, or a completed Liandry's
because the 4 seconds of movement
speed that you get, is extended for each
additional tick of individual magic or
true damage.

As well as: bramble vest for similar 
reasons since if they just auto attack 
you once, then you'll get the movement 
speed effect because the magic damage 
you deal from bramble vest counts 
towards cosmic drive.

Also: this item synergizes quite well with
rocketbelt because rocketbelt can procc
the movement speed effect early via the
missiles it creates with it's dash.
This item is viable as a third item.

Don't go Anti-kite items after your third item.

You probably should've went them before your fourth item if you're
having issues with catching up with the enemy team.

Cosmic Drive, as a rush item, can be best
described as:

"Oh god, I need an item to consistently stay
in range, but I don't want to sack the damage
I would be getting from something like shield
bash as opposed to approach velocity which
doesn't provide any damage value at all."

Now, as a first item, I generally don't think it's
that great against a lot of champions simply
because of my view of it being more-so an
enabler for damage items like Riftmaker or
Dusk & Dawn via it's an insane amount of
ability haste.

However, I do occassionally build as a rush 
item when I'm going against Aatrox players
who specifically rush Maw Of Malmortius or
Akali / Gragas players where I'd rather 
have the combat pressure that comes 
with shield bash as opposed to the anti-kite 
gained from a setup such as Rylai's with 
approach velocity.

I run this setup into Maw Of Malmortius Aatrox
because my gameplan into that specific setup
relies on outkiting his abilities via my movement
speed and consequently outkiting his Maw of 
Malmortius shield so that I can abuse it's 
cooldown.

However, if the Aatrox builds more offensively,
then I will also consequently build more
offensively.

And into Akali / Gragas, I want to maintain
distance against them without sacrificing shield
bash due to the fact that they have relatively
scary all-in power in comparison to a matchup
like Dr. Mundo, Vladimir or Singed.

And Cosmic Drive, is barely enough movement
speed to consistently keep up with them while
greeding for a shield bash oriented rune setup.

Rylai's, by itself, is a lot more viable as a
second or third item because it sets up
abilities,

Now, the most obvious application of this
is to setup your own abilities, but if you're
good enough, you won't need for that.

The less obvious application of this item
in your second or third item slot is to setup
your teammates' abilities such as Miss 
Fortune Ultimate for example.

Additionally: this item synergizes quite 
well with rocketbelt because 
rocketbelt can procc the slow effect early 
via the missiles it creates with it's dash.
This item is viable as a third item.

Don't go Anti-kite items after your third item.

You probably should've went them before your fourth item if you're
having issues with catching up with the enemy team.

Start at Riftmaker or 
Dusk & Dawn

Before going this item

If you really hate one person in particular
on the enemy team and require a mix of
mobility and damage, then Experimental
Hexplate is a really good option.

Do note that this item will run it's course
as soon as you finish ulting somebody,

So if you want consistent movement speed
versus a multitude of enemies, and don't
mind sacrificing a bit of overall DPS, then
I'd recommend going Cosmic Drive 
instead.
This item is viable as a third item.

Damage items are always viable throughout the entire game,
as 3rd+ items, however if you need any form of utility, 

Build that instead.

Start at Riftmaker or 
Dusk & Dawn

Before going this item

If you need a burst damage option towards
a multitude of squishier units, as opposed
to hard focusing against one unit (Like how
Dusk & Dawn works),

Then I'd recommend going Hextech
Gunblade as a second item due to it's 
high synergy with Mordekaiser's hybrid 
scalings on his Q.

It also helps that the slow is pretty nice
for anti-kite and consequently for setting
up your E.

Though, that's mostly just an added bonus.

Additionally: the added omnivamp is more 
efficient here, if you are building it against
a lot of squishier units, because you're
dealing a lot of burst damage which
consequently heals you a lot more.

If the enemies are tankier, however, it's
more efficient to build an item that is
better at taking down tankier units as the
applied damage is going to be higher
due to your item's anti-tank properties as
opposed to Hextech Gunblade's burst
oriented properties, even with it's added
omnivamp healing.
This item is viable as a third item.

Damage items are always viable throughout the entire game,
as 3rd+ items, however if you need any form of utility, 

Build that instead.
Damage Items

As a damage item, Riftmaker's best use case
is to combat opponents where the fights are
guaranteed to be long where you can maximize
the amplifcation damage and omnivamp gained
from the item.

I used to go Liandry's rush into tankier 
matchups, however: ever since the AP nerfs to 
Liandry's, I feel like it's not nearly as viable as 
a rush item compared to Riftmaker, just purely 
because of how more powerful the stronger 
amp and omnivamp is.
This item is viable as a second item.
This item is viable as a third item.

Damage items are always viable throughout the entire game,
as 3rd+ items, however if you need any form of utility, 

Build that instead.

As a damage item, Dusk & Dawn's best use 
case is to combat opponents where the fights
are guaranteed to be relatively short,

Now, this usually comes because the enemy is
either relatively squishy or they have an 
exceptionally large amount of burst that is 
hard to deal with.

Consequently, when it comes to these specific
champions, they also are packaged with an
insane amount of close-combat mobility,
think: Yasuo, Yone, Irelia, Sylas, Ambessa, etc.

These champions excel at being directly at
your face which makes landing skillshots
difficult against them.

Luckily for us, Dusk & Dawn only requires you
to auto attack them to procc it's item effect 
as it's nature as a sheen item pertains.

As to why it's so powerful as a burst item tool,
Mordekaiser's passives (yes, there are two of
them), both get activated from Dusk &
Dawn with the on-hit passive being a pseudo
Nashor's tooth being applied twice all at once,
which consequently deals a lot of damage,

And Mordekaiser's damaging circle (the more
noticeable effect) gets it's stacks procc'd
quicker.

Which are both exceptionally strong effects.
This item is viable as a second item.
This item is viable as a third item.

Damage items are always viable throughout the entire game,
as 3rd+ items, however if you need any form of utility, 

Build that instead.

Liandry's got nerfed too hard
to be a viable rush item for Morde

Just go Riftmaker instead.

If you need more anti-tank items, and the
enemy team composition doesn't have
a ridiculously high amount of magic resist,

Then Liandry's is pretty good.
This item is viable as a third item.

Damage items are always viable throughout the entire game,
as 3rd+ items, however if you need any form of utility, 

Build that instead.

Bloodletter's curse as a rush item is only good
against K'sante because he's one of the only
champions in the entire game who heavily
relies on his tank ratios to further increase his
ridiculous damage output.

If you're not going against K'sante, don't rush this item.

If you need more anti-tank items, but the
enemy team composition has a ridiculously 
high amount of magic resist,

Then Bloodletter's curse is pretty good.
This item is viable as a third item.

Damage items are always viable throughout the entire game,
as 3rd+ items, however if you need any form of utility, 

Build that instead.

I personally don't like going Zhonya's 
second, unless I'm in one of two scenarios:

1. I'm going against an Olaf top and I'm
rushing this item to specifically time out
his ultimate.

Especially because phase rush is being 
removed; this is basically your only way of 
countering him effectively or:

2. I'm getting jumped by the entire
enemy team to such a ridiculous agree 
that I can't even setup my core 1-2 items 

(Which should generally either be anti-kite
or damage items as previously mentioned)

This is usually my go-to answer to the
situation where I'm getting repeatedly
jumped outside of my ultimate,

Because if they proceed to try that strat
against me when I have this item, I can
safely procc my passive before leaving
my ultimate and then consequently
Zhonya's -> DPS the enemy team while
they wait for me to get out of Zhonya's
to kill me again.

This is is assuming no one on your team
decides that they want to try and help
you during this time, but even then:
you should have been able to chunk
the enemies relatively hard due to the fact
that you got your core 1-2 items.

(Which should generally either be anti-kite
or damage items).

There is a caveat to this, which can be
solved by building the other items listed
under this item for anti-burst:

You have to actually be able to react to
their damage, because if you can't, then
you'll just die without ever having the ability
to prevent said burst damage, which 
sucks.

Additionally: Combining this item with
Death's dance is exceptional valuable
since Death's dance's "Ignore Pain" 
passive will deal 0 damage to you 
while you're in stasis.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

If you have to deal with an absolutely 
absurd amount of magic damage in the
form of burst,

Then go Kaenic Rookern.

Additionally: If you have shield bash, this
item does indeed procc it for additional
dopamine hits.

Also: this item pairs REALLY well
with Spirit Visage as it amps up Kaenic
Rookern's shield to prevent an absolutely
absurd amount of burst damage.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

If you're going against a general amount
of mixed burst damage, and the enemy 
explicitly doesn't have Serpent's Fang,

Then go Sterak's Gage.

Additionally: If you have shield bash, this
item does indeed procc it for additional
dopamine hits.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

If you have to deal with an absolutely 
absurd amount of physical damage in the
form of burst,

Then go Death's Dance.

Additionally: this item isn't susceptible to
Serpent's Fang, unlike the other two items
that are built to counter high amounts of
burst damage that are hard to react to
which is pretty nice.

Also: Combining this item with
Zhonya's Hourglass is exceptional 
valuable since Death's dance's "Ignore 
Pain" passive will deal 0 damage to you 
while you're in stasis.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

itemguide.title: Tank Items (That aren't explicitly for anti-burst)

slots.text: Go Randuin's if there's a lot of Crit damage
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

Spirit Visage is really good if you're not
taking too much magic damage 
(whether that be from lots of DOT or burst),
but still have to build magic resistance for 
somebody on the enemy team.

Or: if you have an enchanter on your team
that is doing a really good job at keeping
you alive.

Because: not only when you build this item,
are you amping up your healing from every
single source you currently have,

(Like: Riftmaker or Conqueror healing or,
as previously mentioned, an enchanter)

But you are also increasing your potential
offense with shield bash ( if you have it )
via the shield amp.

It's a bit of a greedy item in my opinion,
but oh~ when the situation calls for it, it's
absolutely godlike.

Additionally: this item pairs REALLY well
with Kaenic Rookern as it amps up it's
shield to prevent an absolutely absurd
amount of burst damage.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

I only go Force Of Nature as a second item
if I'm specifically going against a lane 
opponent that applies a lot of magic 
damage over time such as Cassiopeia or
Singed,

However, there is a condition to this and 
that is if the enemy composition doesn't
have any other form of magic damage 
dealer, then I instead tend to opt into
Riftmaker and deal with the fact that I'm
not going to be nearly as strong in the 1v1.

As a third+ item, Force Of Nature is really
good if you're taking a lot of magic 
damage over time, such as if you're going
against a lot of Liandry's users or users
who have built-in DOT into their kits,

Such as Singed, Cassiopeia, Brand, etc.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

Abyssal Mask is really good if
you're both:

- Often surrounded by enemies that deal
high amounts of magic damage,

- And if your team also has a high amounts
of magic damage
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

Go Frozen Heart if there's a lot of attack
speed oriented champions on the enemy
team.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

Usually, I don't tend to finish Bramble vest
into a finished Thornmail, just because if
there's a lot of healing on the enemy team,

I'd rather just go Oblivion orb and 
consequently: Morellonomicon to apply
anti-healing consistently towards a variety
of enemies,

But: If I'm limiting myself to ulting one 
specific target and they heal via auto 
attacks or some variation of an on-hit
ability, then I'll sometimes finish Thornmail.

Additionally: If I also have a cosmic drive,
which makes it so that if I apply any form
of magic damage, I'll be able to get a 
speed boost, then I'll sometimes opt into
building Thornmail, purely for that one
specific interaction.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

Only build Jak'sho, if you have:

- A lot of pre-established tank items,

- The ability to live long enough to stack 
Jak'sho; don't go Jak'sho vs.a lot of 
burst damage, but rather: if you're going
against a lot of sustained damage.

- And there's a bunch of magic and 
phyiscal damage on the enemy team who
are both equally threatening
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

I only build Unending despair if:

- The enemy team, when they jump me 
after my ultimate, doesn't immediately
one-shot me.

- And if I have some form of amplifcation
damage to further increase Unending
Despair's damaging-healing effect

- And also if they have a good amount of
physical damage dealers.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

Go Deadman's Plate if you're having 
trouble dealing with a lot of slows on the
enemy team, even with the anti-kite items
mentioned up above.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

Dark seal's almost always a good item pickup

It's low-cost, it's gold efficient, and it stacks
really quickly because of all of your AOE 
abilities in teamfights.

You can't really go wrong with buying this item
early
This item is viable as a second item.
This item is viable as a third item.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

Mejai's, is a REALLY risky item to go
towards since it can completely throw a
game if you play cards incorrectly.

Yes, the 10% bonus movement speed is
strong, yes the stacking AP is insanely
overpowered.

But if you die with it, you're losing so much
gold value that you could've went with
a different item.

So, before buying Mejai's you should
keep the following principles in mind:

1. Is there someone who's really fed on
the enemy team who you both have to
deal with, and they have the potential
to kill you? (If yes, then don't go Mejai's)

2. Do you have flash up and/or Zhonya's 
to maintain your Mejai's stacks? 
(If not, then don't go Mejai's).

3. Are you the main frontliner when it
comes to clearing vision and/or do you
have no vision control because your team
is behind? (If yes, then don't go Mejai's or 
play exceptionally cautiously).

Having one scenario be present is fine,
but I'd generally avoid Mejai's if there are
2 or more scenarios present in whatever
game you find yourself in.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

If there's an excessive amount of healing
on the enemy team who aren't specifically
auto attacking you,

Then go Oblivion Orb (and later: 
Morellonomicon) to cut said healing 
towards a variety of enemies via your 
AOE abilities.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

If you are looking to ambush a target in
the mid-game with a key skillshot that
will halt your approach,

Then Verdant barrier (and later: 
Banshee's Veil), is a viable option.

The only reason why I don't like building
this item earlier is because it delays your
item powerspikes and can easily be 
procc'd in sustained and controlled 
environments, such as laning phase.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

If your only goal in the game you're playing
in is to stall and specifically annoy one
enemy player in particular, 

Then I'd recommend going Guardian's
Angel to prolong your time with them in
the death realm, even after you die.

(For extra annoying points: combine this
with a Zhonya's Hourglass to be even
more infuriating!)
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

If the enemy team has a lot of shields, but
for some reason your team doesn't want
to build Serpent's Fang,

And when you explicitly asked them to buy
it, they refused to.

Then, I GUESS- you can go Serpent's 
Fang (even though the lethality is 
completely wasted for you).

Like, I know that you're able to apply it
pretty to a large amount of people with 
your AOE abilities, but seriously?

Nobody else on your teams to build it???
Honestly, I'd report them.
This item is viable as a fourth+ item.

Buy this vs. champions with high amounts of 
auto attacking damage.

Please don't delay tier 2 boots past your first item,

Unless you can fully buy a dedicated anti-kite item like rocketbelt to make up for it.

Buy this vs. champions with high amounts of 
crowd control / roots / stuns.

Buy this if you're snowballing and you don't
need any of the boots above.

I personally don't run boots of swiftness that
often for the sake of opportunity cost,

But it's pretty good against compositions with
a lot of slows.

The idea behind going grasp is to further
enchance your excessively short trades against
certian champions like Riven or Tryndamere.

( Also: credits to Artistic Turtle for discovering
this and applying in EUW Grandmasters )
yo

Shield bash AKA: my wife, is the only rune that you should go if you're opting into the resolve tree

It's great for burst damage via your W or if you buy Sterak's Gage, and: it additionally synergizing with any potential 
enchanters on your team, so that's pretty cool.

Also: it makes a funny dopamine sound, and that's plenty of a good reason to use it.

This is really good if you're going against a 
matchup that pokes you a lot.

This is really good if you're going against a
matchup that has to force itself to all-in you

and has no way of proccing said rune early.

This is great for if you're going against 
compositions that require you to survive an
initial burst amount of damage; you can't get
too much value from Conqueror healing
or Riftmaker healing or multiple W procc's.

Generally, I only go this rune if I'm going 
against a matchup that is hard to all-in against,
but also has the capabilities to break down
bone plating relatively easily.

Personally, I don't tend to go Unflinching that
often unless I'm going a composition that
has CC in every single one of their champion's kits.

The idea behind going PTA is to solely rely
on auto attacks and raw burst damage to take
out any excessively slippery foe such as:
Fiora, Vayne, or Ambessa.

Now: by itself, at least: before your first item,
this is relatively poor compared to grasp when
it comes to situating yourself to exclusively
short trades.

However, when you do get Dusk & Dawn,
that's when this item's burst potential truly 
shines as instead of PTA proccing in three
auto attacks, it now can procc on two auto
attacks.

Which is really nice when your only form of 
consistent damage against these champions
are auto attacks.

( Also: credits to Tjake and Artistic Turtle for
discovering this tech and applying said tech
in EUW Grandmasters )

Conqueror is regarded as Mordekaiser's best
general rune for good reason, and that is 
because: 

Not only do you stack it relatively quickly 
and relatively safely within your ultimate,

But the actual effects; generally increased
damage and more importantly: the healing
gained from said rune is exceptionally 
important for Mordekaiser, especially because
of his wide AOE attacks via his passive, his
Q, and his E.

If you're ever giving up this rune for an 
alternative source of damage, utility or mobility, 

It better be for a good reason.

This rune got nerfed too hard to be good in any
setup when it comes to the precision tree.

This rune just takes way too long to stack up and it's
rewards for when you do stack it up are canceled out
by Mordekaiser's long channel animations.

I know Federals123 likes to run this rune into Irelia to
solely focus on auto attacks while also not limiting 
himself to Dusk & Dawn, but personally:

I think limiting yourself to Rylai's with approach velocity
is an even worse approach simply due to the fact that
Rylai's, as an item, doesn't provide any actual combat
stats and is instead: a setup tool for whatever ability
you need your teammates to land.

And it's not like Irelia is a pushover where you can
almost never win a 1v1; the Irelia has plenty of ways
of outplaying you, 

Which is why I personally prefer going alternative setups 
that focus more-so on damage without suffering from 
the opportunity cost of not going PTA for amplification 
damage or Conqueror for healing, because again:
Lethal tempo takes way too long to stack and is
contradictory to Mordekaiser's relatively long 
ability channel animations.

I know some Mordekaiser players like to run
absorb life into more voltaile lanes,

But ever since the nerfs they did to the rune,
I just feel like the scaling from Triumph is way
too valuable to give up.

This is easily one of Mordekaiser's best 
minor runes purely because of how easy
it is to procc the 2.5% of your maximum health 
(+ 5% of your missing health) healing on 
takedown from your AOE abilities.

If you know it's pretty hard to consistently hit
skillshots against the enemy team comp;
if there are a lot of squishier fighters / 
skirmishers on the enemy team,

Then Legend: Alacrity is pretty good.

If you know you're able to consistently hit
skillshots against the enemy tank; if the enemy
tank has a lot of beefy tanks, 

Then Legend: Haste is pretty good.

If the enemy has an mechanic that makes them
extremely dangerous when they are at low HP,

Then I'd recommend going Coup de Grace.

If the enemy laner has an execute, I'd 
recommend going Cut Down.

For the precision tree, assuming the enemy 
doesn't have an explicit mechanic for if they
are low hp that is exceptionally dangerous,

Or if the enemy doesn't have an execute,

Then this is your best rune when it comes down 
to raw DPS.

Great for poke, but....
Go Deathfire Touch instead.

This rune is really reliant on the enemy NOT
explictly dodging your arcane comet by
moving away slowly; it's just not worth going.

Go Deathfire Touch instead.

This is Phase Rush's replacement, now:

My personal theory behind this rune is that if
you're able to initially get in range of a ranged
unit (in which you can easily procc the 25% 
maximum health requirement because of how
squishy they are), but struggle consistently 
maintaining range, 

I think this is Mordekaiser's best rune choice 
for that specific scenario.

(Examples: Twisted Fate, Smolder, Quinn, etc.)

This rune is Mordekaiser's best choice when
it comes down to raw poke damage.

Especially when you consider the fact that
it actually outdamages Conqueror during the earlier 
stages and later stages of a game

( You can see the math below this entry )

In the mid-game: Conqueror still deals more damage,
but do consider the fact that Conqueror has healing
attached to it, so I still think Conqueror is better in
certain scenarios like if you're going against a tank
or something.

But again: in matchups where your main goal is to
solely poke out the enemy, this is your best option.

This rune is only really good for reducing
your ult cooldown, but to be honest: the 
movement speed that you get from nimbus 
cloak is too good for if you're running this tree.

This is (in my opinion), Mordekaiser's best
minor rune when it comes to the sorcery tree,

Not only are you getting more CDR to apply
your abilities onto enemies through levels 5
and 8,

But: at level 11: you get an additional effect
where your abilities refund 20% of their current
cooldown assuming you get a takedown,
which is extremely good on Mordekaiser 
because of how easy it is to apply AOE effects 
onto individuals in a teamfight via your passive,
your Q, or your E.

In other words: if you're not planning on hard
focusing on poke and getting a lead through
that specific game-plan:

This is your one of your best options when it
comes to raw scaling, especially since it isn't
reliant on game time like how Absolute Focus is.

I'd imagine this only good if you're
synergistically applying with Stormraider's 
Surge or waterwalking if you want to hard
focus on roaming.

Generally though, I'd prefer either 
Transcendence or Absolute Focus for scaling
or poke. ( Especially because Phase Rush is
gone right now )

If you want to hard focus onto raw poke damage,
for a specific matchup, this is not that bad of an
option in my opinion.

Although: Generally, I'd prefer going 
Transcendance purely because of its 
potential as a kill-resetting (and consequently) 
game-breaking effects.

(See the entry on Transcendance for more info)

top laners as you could go Teleport and Ghost
for the laning phase, while also having things 
such as cleanse or flash for the later stages 
of the game.

And now that phase rush is out of the game,
I'd imagine this rune will have a resurgance
against ranged top laners where it's difficult to
get into range to procc anything to begin with
such as artillery units like Xerath, Vel'koz, or
Ziggs.

In which case, you can either use Ghost or
cleanse or whatever other ability to assist with
getting into range.
